intended_object: The canonical bijection from the "Ind-Yoneda lemma". For a diagram D : I ⥤ Cᵒᵖ (so i ↦ D(i)ᵒᵖ is a contravariant diagram in C) and a presheaf F on C, Hom(colim_i y(D_i), F) ≅ lim_i F(D_i), with universes lifted. Inferred from the docstring and the name, alongside the sibling covariant and Pro-Coyoneda versions in the same file.
explanation:
The body composes two isomorphisms:
- `colimitHomIsoLimitYoneda'`, which turns Hom(colim_i yoneda(D_i), F) into the limit of the functor i ↦ (yoneda(D_i) ⟶ F);
- a limit isomorphism induced by the Yoneda lemma `yonedaLemma C`, which identifies (yoneda(X) ⟶ F) with uliftFunctor(F(X)) naturally in X and F. This is restricted along `D ⋙ Prod.sectL`, which fixes F.

The result is Hom(colim y∘D.leftOp, F) ≅ lim (D ⋙ F ⋙ ulift). That is exactly the standard statement that maps out of a colimit of representables are the limit of the evaluations of F.

The generality is the natural one: C is an arbitrary category, I is an arbitrary index category, F is an arbitrary presheaf, and the only hypotheses are that the relevant colimit and limits exist. The universe lift is needed because the Hom-type lives in a larger universe than F's values.

This is a standard canonical isomorphism, not an auxiliary device. The file's other declarations are variants of it (covariant, op/unop and Pro-Coyoneda versions), not more general forms.
